children: The eurozone's Sentix indicator, a gauge of investor confidence, fell in November, pointing to subdued growth in the fourth quarter, Oxford Economics' Iain Simmons says in a note. Expectations weakened for a second straight month, while current conditions were unchanged. "The release adds to signals that this summer's upswing in surveys has lost some of its steam, consistent with the moderation in October's PMIs and ESI," Simmons says. Still, the fall was modest, pointing to subdued rather than deteriorating confidence, he adds. Data for Germany was a bright spot as the industrial recovery gains traction, but weaker global sentiment, rising energy costs and higher interest rates threaten to weigh on the eurozone outlook. "Overall, we continue to expect modest Eurozone growth of 0.1% quarter-over-quarter in 4Q." (don.forbes@wsj.com)
